newsitem.title: UK: Epic to meet EBRD on Ukraine gas project.
newsitem.headline: Epic to meet EBRD on Ukraine gas project.

text.p: A delegation from Calgary-based Epic Energy Inc will discuss the financing of a gas project in Ukraine with the representative of the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) in Kiev on Thursday, the company said.

The meeting follows Epic's completion earlier this month of a private placement of 20 million special warrants for C$20 million, allowing the company to pursue its oil and gas development projects in Ukraine's Crimean peninsula.

Ronald Cormick, President and CEO of Epic, said the finance will be used to drill up to 200 shallow production wells around the Aktash field on Crimea's Kerch peninsula, to expand existing transport and storage infrastructure, and to drill more exploratory shallow wells.

And part of the finance will be used to undertake feasibility studies on two or three existing Ukrainian-drilled wells, to evaluate the potential of deeper oil and condensate gas fields. Most of the financing comes from Canadian mutual funds looking for long term investments, Cormick said.

Epic completed test drilling at the Aktash field in June, and by August was producing enough oil with its joint venture partner, Krymgeologia, to cover local operating costs. The low-paraffin, low-sulphur crude with an API gravity of 23 to 25 degrees is now refined at the Lviv refinery in western Ukraine, but from early next year Cormick expects production to rise to 7,000 barrels per day (bpd), and crude will then be available for export to Greece, he said.

As well as oil, the Crimea has highly promising gas reserves, according to Cormick. "The gas fields are directly on a trend with the large gas fields around Krasnodar (in Russia), which already have three trillion feet of gas and 200 million barrels of liquids".
He added that the Crimea has the same sediments and geological history as the Krasnodar area, and initial test holes suggest they have the same potential.

"All drilled areas are productive", he said. "You can't drill a structure there without finding hydrocarbons". The region contains a large section of organic marine shale at depth, he added, and the shales are layered in shallow horizons, packed tight and effectively sealing in the hydrocarbons.

Epic has no plans to market the gas outside Ukraine, unlike the oil. But Cormick is excited about the prospects for gas sales in the country. "The Black Sea basin is a new, very exciting territory", he said. "It has the capacity to make Ukraine self-sufficient in gas".

Infrastructure is already in place, he said, bringing gas onto the Crimean peninsula from Russia and Turkmenistan. Completing the pipeline to the Kerch peninsula and reversing the flow will not be a difficult project.

And there is a disused nuclear power station in the area, built to the same design as the Chernobyl station and taken out of commission at the time of the disaster there, which is now being converted with public sector finance to run on oil and coal. It is to discuss raising finance to switch this to run on gas that Epic is meeting the EBRD on Thursday. Cormick says the bank has already made a preliminary commitment to provide finance once Epic is ready to develop the gas.
